claims.claim: Meta's October 15 announcement releases downloadable multimodal Muse Spark Open weights and hosted access, specifying 816B total parameters, 42B active per token and a 1M-token context window; these specifications and deployment descriptions are company statements.
contradictions: The Muse Model License has limited commercial terms, not unrestricted open-source rights.
Meta's desktop claim concerns two M5 Ultra Mac Studios, not ordinary consumer hardware; downloadable weights do not establish affordable deployment.

claims.claim: Vals reports Muse Spark Open at 46.61% ±1.20 on its Index and 61.34% ±2.09 on Finance Agent v2, with sharply different task rankings.
contradictions: Dossier snapshot ranks are 38/49 and 3/79; the later supplied page excerpt shows 39/50 and 3/80 with unchanged scores. Both snapshots are disclosed, not treated as identical.
Task- and configuration-specific results neither establish general superiority nor directly refute Meta's narrower US open-weight comparison.

claims.claim: DeepSeek's change log dates V4.1-Flash-1017 to October 17; supplied operational documentation routes deepseek-flash and retired deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp names to that checkpoint, with the legacy calls billed at the Flash price.
contradictions: Successful supplied-page retrieval was followed by a failed web retrieval; no complete later-page check is claimed.

claims.claim: Anthropic's October 15 evaluator announcement, clarified October 16, says employee-like METR access has begun; six METR staff received company hardware, office space and internal access roughly comparable to Anthropic risk-assessment teams. Ars reports the implementation while attributing access scope to Anthropic.
contradictions: Onboarding is not evidence of a completed assessment, unrestricted architectural access or release-veto authority.
No newly inspected METR findings resolve the four disclosed cyber incidents or establish incident-discovery coverage.

support.name: Anthropic evaluator access and publication terms

contradictions: Named exclusions include customer data, legally privileged information and model architecture information.

claims.claim: Anthropic's October 18 announcement commits 5% of shares subject to stockholder approval, with discretionary additional 2% allocations for each 50% increase in company value above a baseline; it describes a wholly owned LLC and excludes lobbying and political giving from equity held there.
contradictions: A pledge subject to approval is not a completed transfer, cash distribution or direct public share ownership.
Complete implementation conditions were not established; further governance and valuation-milestone details are promised in coming months.

claims.claim: Anthropic says the new fund commitment combined with earlier founder and employee commitments dedicates roughly 20% of shares to public good before possible valuation-linked additions.
contradictions: Roughly 20% is cumulative, not the new allocation.
No inspected evidence establishes payouts, an enforceable implementation timetable or an AI-safety effect.

claims.claim: The Guardian reports TTP downloaded 135 apps with nudification or nude-body face-swapping features using four accounts identifying users as 13, two Apple and two Google; the report describes access despite parental controls and inaccurate age ratings.
contradictions: The original TTP report was not separately inspected and the supplied Guardian article is truncated.
Four accounts are not a population estimate; researchers used AI-generated images of women rather than photographs of real people.
Apple disputes that some listed apps have nudification or deepfake capabilities, according to the supplied Guardian source check; this capability dispute was not independently resolved.

claims.claim: Google told the Guardian it suspended violating apps and restricted related search terms; the article reports Apple strengthened moderation guidelines after TTP sought comment.
contradictions: Removal completeness and subsequent effectiveness remain unverified; no inspected follow-up retests access after the changes.

claims.claim: DeepSeek's documented stable-name checkpoint migration supports distinguishing API compatibility from model identity; recording backend identity and evaluation configuration is an engineering recommendation, not a completed local evaluation.
contradictions: The invoice example is explicitly illustrative, not an observed model result.
Format validity does not establish factual correctness, authorized action or task success; no local regression or economics measurement was performed.

claims.claim: Across the selected weight-release, evaluator-access, equity-pledge and app-enforcement cases, access or a commitment remains distinct from demonstrated operational outcomes; this is an editorial early signal, not a measured industry trend.
contradictions: The cases concern different mechanisms and do not establish a causal relationship or quantitative trend.
Concrete access implementation and reported platform remediation are real developments, not evidence of no progress.
